candidates.evidence_text: For many teenagers awaiting their GCSE results on Thursday, sitting their exam papers took place over several weeks - but for one 16-year-old from Cheshire, the whole process took months while they used their eye-gaze to answer the questions Patrick, 16, has cerebral palsy and completed his exams over the course of five months using eye-tracking technology As a student at The Fallibroome Academy, in Macclesfield, Patrick began filling out exam papers for his seven GCSEs in February and completed them in June Ahead of results day Patrick told BBC Breakfast : "My ultimate dream is to work in media and to be the next Claire Balding on wheels." Patrick said he was inspired after seeing the late Rob Burrow, a rugby league player who had motor neurone disease (MND), appear on an episode of CBeebies Bedtime Stories, narrating the story using a computer to speak Patrick, who also uses a computer to speak, was able to complete his exams by using eye-gaze tracking technology

candidates.lead: Victim Support helped Trish through court proceedings after sexual abuse she suffered as a child
candidates.evidence_text: Droylsden dad boxes to raise £2k after charity helped his wife - BBC News Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig says seeing Trish go through the court process made him want to give something back to Victim Support By Haider Saleem North West Published 1 hour ago A father who had never boxed has raised £2,630 for a charity supporting people affected by crime - after it helped his wife through court proceedings over sexual abuse she suffered as a child. Craig Hinde, 41, from Droylsden, Greater Manchester, trained for eight weeks before taking part in a white-collar boxing event in Manchester. His wife Trish said Victim Support prepared her for court after she reported being sexually abused as a child by her father, Gerard King, who was convicted at Chester Crown Court in 2022. Craig also said it had helped their son Jacob, 10, who took up boxing after being bullied, regain his sparring confidence, showing how trying mattered more than winning. Trish, 38, said she had never been in a courtroom before and described the prospect as "terrifying". The lettings administrator said Victim Support talked her through what to expect and reassured her that it was acceptable to say she did not know or could not remember an answer. "For people who have been through trauma, they often are terrified of not being believed," she said. But she said there was none of that feeling when speaking to the charity. "It's just acceptance and validation," she said. "There's no judgment. They just help you through the process." Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig said he had avoided physical exercise since injuring his knees at 17 Trish said getting help was "the best thing I ever did" and that she was now a very different person from the one who had gone through the court process. She said hearing somebody acknowledge how awful her experience had been changed the way she thought about what had happened. "For somebody to just say, what happened to you was awful, it just changes something in your brain," she said. Craig said watching his wife go through the case had been extremely difficult: "There's not much I could do, like it was out of my hands" he said. Craig said he had not known about Victim Support until his family needed its help. "You don't know you need them until you need them," he said. He said the charity told him it had "never done this before" when he approached it about raising money through white-collar boxing. Craig said he initially thought raising £50 or £100 would be a good result, but eventually collected £2,630 and was named the event's Golden Glove Top Fundraiser. He trained at ISAN Gym in Oldham and said he had never boxed before signing up. Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Craig and Trish say they noticed Jacob's confidence in boxing improve after his father's challenge Craig said Jacob had taken up boxing and the sport had helped him through bullying. However, his son later became hesitant about sparring and Craig wanted to show him that putting himself in an uncomfortable situation was an achievement regardless of whether he won. Jacob was too young to attend the event, but Craig said he showed him footage afterwards. Craig narrowly lost the contest but said: "It was just the getting in there that counted." He said he noticed "a big switch" in Jacob's confidence in the following weeks and that his son had since started technical sparring. Image source, Craig Hinde Image caption, Trish says she was proud that Victim Support was the first charity Craig thought of when deciding where the money should go Craig's training also coincided with the deaths of both his grandparents within days of each other. He said his grandmother died on a Saturday and his grandfather, whom he described as a role model, died the following Monday. Craig said he sat crying in his car before that evening's training session and questioned whether to go inside. "I got tears in the car before I got in there, wiped them," he said. He decided to train and said afterwards: "My head just felt lighter." Craig said the exercise helped him mentally during what he described as "a real difficult time". He said he had been more nervous about the ring walk than the contest itself, but seeing Trish in the crowd had helped. Reflecting on their family life since the court case, Trish said: "We live very much in the moment now." "We try and enjoy every moment." candidates.evidence_text: A keen rugby player and strongman described by his mother as a "gentle giant" had a prescription for anti-psychotic medication withdrawn weeks before his death, an inquest heard James Snowden, who had struggled with suicidal feelings since childhood, was 21 when his body was found at his family home in Altrincham in December 2024 Manchester South Coroner's Court heard after numerous attempts to take his own life he had been prescribed sulpiride in 2021 - which his mother said had helped him "pursue a full life" When James died he was under the care of the Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, which will give evidence throughout the week and has been approached for comment However, the court heard that on 26 November 2024, James had attended an appointment to plan for the gradual withdrawal of the drug Snowden, a keen sportsman, had been a member of Broughton Park FC and Sale FC Rugby Clubs and St Lawrence's Gaelic Football Club

candidates.evidence_text: Murder inquiry after man dies two days after Manchester stabbing - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, A 29-year-old woman, initially arrested on suspicion of wounding, has been further detained on suspicion of murder By Jonny Humphries North West Published 17 August 2026 A murder investigation has been launched after a man died two days after he was stabbed in the leg. The 36-year-old was found injured at a house on Berwyn Avenue in Blackley, Manchester, at 02:45 BST on Saturday following reports of a disturbance. He was taken to hospital but died from his injuries on Monday morning. A 29-year-old woman, who was initially arrested on suspicion of wounding and assaulting a police officer, was now being questioned on suspicion of murder, Greater Manchester Police said. The force previously said the police officer was not seriously hurt. Det Insp Terina Arthern said the suspect and victim were known to each other and described the attack as an "isolated incident" with "no threat to the wider community". "I would like to express my sincere condolences to the victim in this case," she said. "We have informed his next-of-kin and our thoughts remain with his family and friends. "Our investigation has been moving at pace since the weekend to establish the facts." candidates.summary: The foam was left-over "run-off" from the foam firefighters used to tackle a large blaze on Sunday

candidates.lead: The foam was left-over "run-off" from the foam firefighters used to tackle a large blaze on Sunday
candidates.evidence_text: Hundreds of fish die after foam pollutes Oldham river - BBC News Image source, Craig Hannah Image caption, The foam was left-over "run-off" from the foam firefighters used to tackle a large blaze on Sunday By Georgie Docker North West Published 17 August 2026 Hundreds of fish have been found dead after a fire at an industrial unit caused masses of foam to run into a nearby river. The fish were found in the River Tame following the blaze off Wellington Road in Greenfield, on Sunday, The Environment Agency said. The foam was described by the agency as "firewater run off", which is left-over from the foam firefighters used to tackle the fire. A spokesperson said: "Although containment measures were taken, some firewater run-off entered the river. Officers recorded several hundred dead fish in the affected area, however this morning they found no additional fish fatalities." The spokesperson continued: "Surface foam remains visible. However, it appears to be dispersing downstream. "We will continue to monitor the situation and assess any ongoing environmental impacts." Image source, Craig Hannah Image caption, Swathes of foam were spotted in the River Tame Craig Hannah, 57, lives close by and witnessed the blaze- which began just after 07:30 BST on Sunday. "It was quite frightening. I live around 70 metres away from it. Luckily we were downwind," he said. "It was just the road closures, the proximity to other people's houses that was quite worrying." Residents have since returned to their homes, but Craig said there was alarm at the state of the river. "I went for a walk earlier as I often do and was downstream from where the fire had happened and you couldn't help but notice the amount of foam on the surface of the river," he said. "It was probably about four metres high in the worst affected areas. "It had got caught up in the trees." Image source, Craig Hannah Image caption, The foam was about four metres high in places Craig said he could see the foam was breaking down. "It was slowly fragmenting away a bit like icebergs in the Antarctic," he said. "Sections would break off and then float down and catch up again." Image source, Craig Hannah Image caption, The foam appeared to break down as it travelled downstream "It makes me feel sad," the former countryside warden continued. "When I first started working a few miles downstream from Greenfield in 1988, you were very unlikely to see fish in the river," he said. "But fish live in the river all the way down to Stockport now. "The wildlife's come back and it's quite a dynamic ecosystem. "I just really hope that this incident hasn't had a major impact on what is now in the river." candidates.lead: The council says work will begin as soon as possible if the scheme is approved this autumn
candidates.evidence_text: Long-awaited plans to transform a major public space in the centre of a city have been submitted Ten months on from the proposals first being revealed, Manchester City Council has put in a planning bid to create more lawns, plant more trees and create a larger playground for families in Piccadilly Gardens The authority said work could begin "as soon as possible" if planning permission was granted in the autumn Hundreds of people responded to a consultation on the plans, with some raising concerns about continued anti-social behaviour at the site, and questioning how it would be kept safe for those who would want to use it Under the plans, old fountains, low concrete walls and raised planters will be removed, while lighting, sightlines and CCTV will be improved Of those who took part in the consultation, 58% believed the proposals would create a safe and welcoming space, 67% said they would provide clear walking routes, and 70% thought they would make it greener and more colourful

candidates.evidence_text: A man has been charged after police ended a two-day stand-off by climbing a ladder to arrest a sleeping suspect on a roof Greater Manchester Police released footage showing the moment an officer climbed the ladder onto the roof of a back porch in Ash Street, Salford, and grabbed a man, who was lying down The man was pulled down the ladder, with his trousers appearing to fall down, before being arrested by officers in the garden of the property on Saturday Simon Harris, 37, has been charged with four counts of criminal damage, two counts of assault of an emergency worker, intentionally/recklessly causing a public nuisance, burglary dwelling and theft He is due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court later Detective Chief Inspector Helen Bagnall thanked members of the public following the man's arrest, which came after a two-day emergency service response

candidates.evidence_text: For many teenagers awaiting their GCSE results on Thursday, sitting their exam papers took place over several weeks - but for one 16-year-old from Cheshire, the whole process took months while they used their eye-gaze to answer the questions Patrick, 16, has cerebral palsy and completed his exams over the course of five months using eye-tracking technology As a student at The Fallibroome Academy, in Macclesfield, Patrick began filling out exam papers for his seven GCSEs in February and completed them in June Ahead of results day Patrick told BBC Breakfast : "My ultimate dream is to work in media and to be the next Claire Balding on wheels." Patrick said he was inspired after seeing the late Rob Burrow, a rugby league player who had motor neurone disease (MND), appear on an episode of CBeebies Bedtime Stories, narrating the story using a computer to speak Patrick, who also uses a computer to speak, was able to complete his exams by using eye-gaze tracking technology

candidates.evidence_text: A keen rugby player and strongman described by his mother as a "gentle giant" had a prescription for anti-psychotic medication withdrawn weeks before his death, an inquest heard James Snowden, who had struggled with suicidal feelings since childhood, was 21 when his body was found at his family home in Altrincham in December 2024 Manchester South Coroner's Court heard after numerous attempts to take his own life he had been prescribed sulpiride in 2021 - which his mother said had helped him "pursue a full life" When James died he was under the care of the Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, which will give evidence throughout the week and has been approached for comment However, the court heard that on 26 November 2024, James had attended an appointment to plan for the gradual withdrawal of the drug Snowden, a keen sportsman, had been a member of Broughton Park FC and Sale FC Rugby Clubs and St Lawrence's Gaelic Football Club

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Nearly 200 new homes could be built in a ‘beautiful’ valley as part of a major new development that includes a new Metrolink stop Plans have been submitted to Oldham Council asking for approval for up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley in Oldham. The scheme is being put forward by IDPartnership Northern on behalf of Barratt Homes Manchester The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. This is a long term plan across every borough in the region except Stockport to oversee housebuilding, create jobs, and protect green belt land from unplanned development In the wider plans for the area, around 2,000 new homes could be built alongside new industrial and warehouse space, a local centre, and new access to education facilities. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road as well as new Metrolink stop at Broadb The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport 'Healthy and active' grandad woke on Christmas Day unable to move When Andy Shaw arrived on the Stockport stroke ward he could barely talk Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 17:52, 17 Aug 2026 View Image Andy Shaw an A healthy and active grandad has told of how he woke up on Christmas Day and collapsed after developing a severe headache the night before Andy Shaw, a former soldier and police officer, was unable to move the left side of his body after suffering the life-threatening stroke in the early hours of December 25, 2022 The 61-year-old, who spent 25 years working in the police force, had gone to bed on Christmas Eve after developing a headache "I went to bed and waited for Santa," Andy says, "But then at 2am, I woke up to go to the toilet and collapsed." As he fell, Andy managed to pull the duvet off his bed, waking his wife Bernadette, who called an ambulance. He was taken to Salford Royal Hospital, where he underwent surgery to remove the blood clot in his brain that was responsible for the stroke - but the operation did not go

He promoted the lines on Snapchat and also with business cards and lighters which contained contac His team of dealers and accomplices mainly targeted university students living in Fallowfield , south Manchester, but they also supplied a vast array of drugs such as cocaine, ecstasy, 2CB and 'magic mushrooms' at large events such as Parklife, Manchester Crown Court was told Police in plain clothes first arrested him in Fallowfield in February 2022 when they spotted him on a mountain bike and detected the smell of cannabis. He denied running the drugs line He was still on bail when he was arrested again in May 2025 after staff at a Travelodge hotel on Ducie Street in Manchester city centre became concerned about the smell of cannabis coming from his room. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Nearly 200 new homes could be built in a ‘beautiful’ valley as part of a major new development that includes a new Metrolink stop Plans have been submitted to Oldham Council asking for approval for up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley in Oldham. The scheme is being put forward by IDPartnership Northern on behalf of Barratt Homes Manchester The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. This is a long term plan across every borough in the region except Stockport to oversee housebuilding, create jobs, and protect green belt land from unplanned development In the wider plans for the area, around 2,000 new homes could be built alongside new industrial and warehouse space, a local centre, and new access to education facilities. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road as well as new Metrolink stop at Broadb The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans

candidates.evidence_text: Bury GMP officers mimicked and mocked accent of black female PC, misconduct hearing told A sergeant is accused of comparing a photo of a suspect to the PC's mother and another PC is alleged to have compared her braided hair to 'a mop' News Paul Britto A group of Greater Manchester Police officers mimicked and mocked the accent of a black female colleague at work then laughed about it, a misconduct hearing was told. It was said to have left the PC feeling 'upset and uncomfortable' The allegations, claim the force, involved 'unwanted, offensive, racist and disrespectful' language and behaviour One, a sergeant, is said to have compared a photograph of a female fraud suspect with curly hair and thick glasses to the PC's mother. The hearing was also told a PC described the officer's braided hair as 'looking like a mop' before smiling at her and walking away Named only as Pc Y, the alleged victim was born in Africa, but speaks fluent English. She joined GMP as a response officer based at Bury police station in May, 2019 The allegations against seven serving officers and two now former officers were made on November 1, 2023. All were based at Bury at the time

Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:51, 17 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Mar A family say they were left stranded on their luxury holiday after their hotel booking was cancelled by a scammer Tania Rowan booked a stay for six people at the Charmillion Club Resort in Egypt through package holiday provider, On the Beach The family from Salford was due to check in on August 5 and return on August 12. According to Tania, the day before she flew out, she was tricked out of £768 after calling a number and speaking to a man who she thought worked for On the Beach Tania, 51, had made the call after she was unable to log onto the On the Beach app to check the status of her booking ahead of the flight. She told the MEN how she found the number on Google with the help of her daughter While on a phone call with a person she presumed to be an On the Beach rep, she was told her account was short of £768

candidates.evidence_text: Blackley 'The street was swarmed with police': Neighbours' shock as man dead and murder investigation launched after stabbing in flat The latest case is now the sixth murder probe in 13 days across Greater Manchester News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter Neighbours on a quiet north Manchester estate have spoken of their shock after a man was confirmed dead and a murder investigation launched on their street Greater Manchester Police said they were called to reports of a disturbance in the early hours of Saturday morning (August 15) on Berwyn Avenue in Blackley Officers found a 36-year-old man at a flat in a residential block with injuries consistent with a stabbing, who was taken to hospital for treatment In an update on Monday (August 17) the force said he had sadly died of his injuries. A single police car remained at the scene on Monday with an officer standing watch outside the block of flats A 29-year-old woman, who was initially arrested on suspicion of wounding and assaulting a police officer, has since been further detained on suspicion of murder and remains in police custody, with GMP's Major Incident Team leading the incident

He denied running the drugs line He was still on bail when he was arrested again in May 2025 after staff at a Travelodge hotel on Ducie Street in Manchester city centre became concerned about the smell of cannabis coming from his room. candidates.evidence_text: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court after a two-day stand-off with police who grabbed the sleeping suspect from a roof Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court. Harris, of no fixed address, who was not legally represented during the five-minute hearing, is accused of six offences between August 14 and 16 The offences include burglary – entering a property in Reservoir Street, Salford , Greater Manchester and stealing T-shirts and rum punch – according to charges read out in court He is also accused of two counts of assaulting an emergency worker – two police officers – intentionally causing a public nuisance by sitting on a roof, and two counts of criminal damage to separate properties Harris entered no pleas to the charges and bail was opposed by prosecutor Hannah Nicholls, who told the court the case was too serious to be dealt with at the magistrates' court

News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:14, 17 Aug 2026 Vie Police investigating an alleged attack where a boy of 15 was stabbed in his back after stepping off a bus are appealing to the public to help trace two people The appeal follows a serious assault on the youngster moments after he stepped off a bus in Gorton at around 11.20pm on Monday June 1. The teen was allegedly attacked by two males The youngster suffered serious injuries 'consistent' with a knife attack, according to Greater Manchester Police . "Thankfully, his injuries were not life-threatening and he has since made a full recovery," the force said in a statement today as officers made their public appeal "One of the suspects is described as a black male, wearing a grey and green Manchester United coat with black trousers," said GMP Officers from GMP's Xcalibre Task Force, set up to tackle gang crime, are now appealing for information following the alleged 'Section 18' assault, also known as grievous bodily harm

The exterior was clad in faience tiles and decorated with Art Deco and Italianate Opened on Christmas Eve 1928 it was one of the first "super cinemas" outside London. It had a huge stage for live variety shows and an orchestra pit It was where Violet Carson's showbiz career began. candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Nearly 200 new homes planned for 'beautiful' Oldham valley alongside new Metrolink stop The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Nearly 200 new homes could be built in a ‘beautiful’ valley as part of a major new development that includes a new Metrolink stop Plans have been submitted to Oldham Council asking for approval for up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley in Oldham. The scheme is being put forward by IDPartnership Northern on behalf of Barratt Homes Manchester The scheme is one of the allocated sites as part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme. This is a long term plan across every borough in the region except Stockport to oversee housebuilding, create jobs, and protect green belt land from unplanned development In the wider plans for the area, around 2,000 new homes could be built alongside new industrial and warehouse space, a local centre, and new access to education facilities. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road as well as new Metrolink stop at Broadb The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans

candidates.evidence_text: Bury GMP officers mimicked and mocked accent of black female PC, misconduct hearing told A sergeant is accused of comparing a photo of a suspect to the PC's mother and another PC is alleged to have compared her braided hair to 'a mop' News Paul Britto A group of Greater Manchester Police officers mimicked and mocked the accent of a black female colleague at work then laughed about it, a misconduct hearing was told. It was said to have left the PC feeling 'upset and uncomfortable' The allegations, claim the force, involved 'unwanted, offensive, racist and disrespectful' language and behaviour One, a sergeant, is said to have compared a photograph of a female fraud suspect with curly hair and thick glasses to the PC's mother. The hearing was also told a PC described the officer's braided hair as 'looking like a mop' before smiling at her and walking away Named only as Pc Y, the alleged victim was born in Africa, but speaks fluent English. She joined GMP as a response officer based at Bury police station in May, 2019 The allegations against seven serving officers and two now former officers were made on November 1, 2023. All were based at Bury at the time

candidates.evidence_text: Piccadilly Gardens Piccadilly Gardens transformation to turn area into 'world-class' destination A planning application has been submitted Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 19:00, 17 Aug 2026 View 3 Images A picture showing how Picca A major revamp of Piccadilly Gardens will turn it into a ‘world-class’ destination, council bosses have said The long-awaited changes at the gardens could be mere months away from starting with a new planning application expected to get the nod of approval by October It is aiming to create a ‘distinctive green heart’ in central Manchester, with Piccadilly Gardens as the ‘front door’ to the city Working with Greater Manchester Police (GMP) and Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), the plans are aiming to shred ‘all the wrong associations’ that Piccadilly Gardens has become known for, particularly around concerns over safety To help with this aim, a new management plan is being drawn up to help the gardens stay 'safe, clean and well-maintained'. This will be done in a partnership between the council, GMP, TfGM, businesses, and residents

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:23, 17 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Strangeways is an area where new homes are planned (Image: Sean Han Manchester’s future until 2039 is about to be decided with a massive development plan getting closer to approval The council’s local plan has mapped out where up to 60,000 new homes will be built around the city, as well as how it will help create new jobs and places for business Places included in a ‘core growth area’ will take the bulk of work and have been earmarked for huge regeneration in future years, accounting for more than 42,000 new homes and 1.4 million sqm of office space This includes central Manchester where there are plans to expand the boundary of the city centre, as well as the areas of Holt Town near Ancoats and New Islington, Central Park near Harpurhey and Newton Heath, Sportcity in east Manchester, and part of the Victoria North project t The core growth area is the ‘economic hub’ of Greater Manchester and is ‘located at the heart of the transport connections across the north of England.’

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Man arrested after 48-hour Salford rooftop stand-off appears in court Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court News John Scheerhout Crime reporter and Pat Hurst Press Association 17:09, 17 Aug 2026 A man has appeared in court after a two-day stand-off with police who grabbed the sleeping suspect from a roof Simon Harris, 37, made a brief appearance in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court. Harris, of no fixed address, who was not legally represented during the five-minute hearing, is accused of six offences between August 14 and 16 The offences include burglary – entering a property in Reservoir Street, Salford , Greater Manchester and stealing T-shirts and rum punch – according to charges read out in court He is also accused of two counts of assaulting an emergency worker – two police officers – intentionally causing a public nuisance by sitting on a roof, and two counts of criminal damage to separate properties Harris entered no pleas to the charges and bail was opposed by prosecutor Hannah Nicholls, who told the court the case was too serious to be dealt with at the magistrates' court

Harris, of no fixed address, who was not legally represented during the five-minute hearing, is accused of six offences between August 14 and 16 The offences include burglary – entering a property in Reservoir Street, Salford , Greater Manchester and stealing T-shirts and rum punch – according to charges read out in court He is also accused of two counts of assaulting an emergency worker – two police officers – intentionally causing a public nuisance by sitting on a roof, and two counts of criminal damage to separate properties Harris entered no pleas to the charges and bail was opposed by prosecutor Hannah Nicholls, who told the court the case was too serious to be dealt with at the magistrates' court

Evidence markers have been placed on the road as investigations are carried out Debris from the crash can be seen scattered across the road within the cordon. A development masterplan was approved by Bury and Rochdale councils in June, setting out their vision for the land Now, the Northern Gateway Development Vehicle LLP, made up of Harworth Estates Investment Ltd and Russell Homes UK, have revealed more information about their intentions for the site The plans remain in the early stages, with just an environmental impact assessment (EIA) scoping request submitted so far. candidates.evidence_text: M6 M6 fully shut for hours after 'very serious' crash as drivers stuck in huge motorway delays An investigation is underway with the motorway closed both ways after the crash near Stoke-on-Trent Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news repor A stretch of the M6 motorway will be fully shut for hours following a 'very serious' crash The crash happened on the northbound carriageway between junctions 15 and 16, near Stoke-on-Trent, at around 4.10am this morning (Monday, August 17). It involved three HGVs and a car, National Highways said The motorway was fully closed in both directions as police, firefighters and paramedics responded. Investigation work will take place on the northbound carriageway throughout the day The closure on this side of the motorway will remain in place into this afternoon. The southbound carriageway was also closed to allow for screens to be put up around the scene and for emergency services access This side of the motorway has since reopened, while the northbound side remains closed as of 10am. There are long queues and delays up to the closure

candidates.evidence_text: Thursday 23 July 2026 at 4:58pm King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court. Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

But now, as NHS treatment options dwindle, Sarah has turned to fundraising for private care Sarah said: “It blew our world apart,” recalling her diagnosis in 2019 She added: “I’ve lived with it now for seven years. I’m eternally grateful to The Christie, but we’ve come to a point now where they can’t offer me anything else under the NHS. candidates.evidence_text: Friday 10 July 2026 at 6:00pm Anthony McGrath accused Andy Burnham of protecting peodophiles. A bomb hoaxer claimed he would target a town hall after accusing Andy Burnham of “protecting paedophiles" and threatening MPs, a court has heard Anthony McGrath, 57, claimed the bombs would arrive from Russia and added: “Stop protecting #paedophiles @AndyBurnhamGM because the town hall will also be removed.” Posting on X in November 2025, McGrath also threatened Greater Manchester Police headquarters unless they returned property belonging to him, Liverpool Crown Court heard on Friday 10 July In January and February 2024 he sent a series of threatening emails to professionals, including Salford MP Rebecca Long-Bailey and Sir Robert Buckland, who at the time was MP for South Swindon, as well as a judge, solicitor, chartered surveyor and Nat West bank strategist McGrath, of Sale, Greater Manchester, was given a community order after the court heard he was suffering with his mental health at the time and had been sectioned following his arrest Martyn Walsh, prosecuting, said in one email sent to Ms Long-Bailey, McGrath said: “You all messed with the wrong person. My army is much bigger considering I have Russian and Chinese support. We will be armed and shoot to kill.”

Credit: Google Maps A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man died in hospital weeks after being stabbed in a "shocking" attack Emergency services were called to Hale Lane in Failsworth at around 9:50pm on Friday, 19 June, following reports of an altercation Steven Dossett was treated for stab wounds at the scene and rushed to hospital. Greater Manchester Police have confirmed that he died from his injuries on Saturday, 4 July Detectives say they are continuing to pursue multiple lines of enquiry Five people - four men and one woman aged between 17 and 45 - were initially arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and assault offences. They have since been released on bail while investigations continue Detective Chief Inspector Anna Barker, the Senior Investigating Officer, said: "This was a shocking attack, which has now evolved into a murder investigation following the death of Steven last week."

candidates.evidence_text: The two buildings on Manchester Road have stood empty since 2020 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has served a formal notice requiring the owners of the derelict Altrincham North Lodge in West Timperley to either substantially repair the building or demolish it and clear the site within six months The former Altrincham North Lodge on Manchester Road, which sits alongside the empty Pelican Inn, has stood empty since 2020 and has become increasingly insecure, prompting repeated concerns from residents and emergency services The latest step follows a fire at the site in April and emergency works in May to board up and fence off the buildings. Those measures reduced the immediate risk of unauthorised access but did not resolve the underlying condition of the Lodge While the council has seen proposals involving the refurbishment of the 1930s mock Tudor Pelican building, designed by local architect George Wescott, it says there appears little prospect of the Lodge being brought back into use Cllr Keleigh Glenton, Trafford Council’s Executive Member for Community Safety and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents have raised concerns about this site for a considerable time and understandably want to see progress

Operating profit increased 8.5% to £10.3m, with EBITDA up 1% to £12.1m The company, which has its headquarters on Atlantic Street in Broadheath, attributed the growth to all channels It opened six new stores during the year, taking the estate to 94 sites, and added two new online marketplaces - George at Asda and Next - taking the total to five. Holland & Barrett and Boots are also based in the area Clare Jennings, Property Director at Superdrug, said in March that they were "excited" to bring "our much-loved health and beauty offer to the heart of the town centre"

candidates.lead: The Local Plan is a guide to development and growth in the city over the next fifteen years and Manchester people are invited to have their say for the final time from today (Monday 17 August)
candidates.evidence_text: The Local Plan is a guide to development and growth in the city over the next fifteen years and Manchester people are invited to have their say for the final time from today (Monday 17 August) The Plan is a legal requirement for every Council to set out a long-term framework about how development should be considered through the planning process, including new housing – as well as affordable homes – green spaces, development that creates employment opportunities, infra The Plan complements a range of strategies and policies that look to deliver the vision of the Council An initial consultation took place in September 2025 starting a process of review and engagement through the last year. This consultation attracted 2,184 responses that have since been considered by planning officers to help update the draft local plan The Local Plan is currently going through Regulation 19, which is the final version of the plan before it is referred to a government inspector for public examination The public will be asked for their comments relating to how ‘workable’ the draft plan is in practice, which is a requirement set out by Government. This ‘test of soundness’ asks the public: does the plan meet its objectives

candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council's Community Safety Service was granted a three-year Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) following repeated offences targeting retailers in Chadderton Athanial Lucas, 30, of no fixed address, appeared before Tameside Magistrates' Court on 29 July charged with three shoplifting offences at Londis in Chadderton Lucas was sentenced to eight weeks in custody, ordered to pay £513 in compensation and made subject to a Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) until 29 July 2029 The three-year CBO was secured by Oldham Council's Community Safety Service, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police. The application detailed 30 reported shoplifting incidents from December 2025, resulting in losses of £3,994 to local businesses Lucas was brought to the attention of the Community Safety Service after retailers reported him for shoplifting up to three incidents a day. candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council has put up over 30 new signs around the town centre to help people find their way around and encourage walking, cycling and wheeling The 34 circular signs are in key locations like Victoria Square, Bradshawgate, Churchgate, Knowsley Street and outside the railway station, where people are most likely to see them They point the way to popular destinations like the Parish church, library and Queens Park, and tell people how long it should take to walk there The new signs also highlight the town hall, Bolton Market, Bolton Lads and Girls Club and the university and colleges Some signs feature motivational messages aimed at encouraging people to get around the town centre on foot, by bike or on scooters The idea is to help people get the health benefits of keeping active, while also reducing traffic congestion by having fewer cars on the road

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

candidates.evidence_text: LGBTQ+ History Guided Tour - Manchester’s Finest LGBTQ+ History Guided Tour Tue 18th Aug, 2026 - Sun 30th Aug, 2026 - Whitworth Locke, Civic Quarter LGBTQ+ History Guided Tour Whitworth Locke, Civic Quarter, 74 Princess St, Manchester M1 6JD Tue 18th Aug, 2026 - Sun 30th Aug, 2026 £11 Get tickets Directions events Go to Manchester's Finest Facebook page Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Discover centuries of LGBTQ+ history on the streets of Manchester through a guided walking tour. As part of SCENE’s Pride programme they’re hosting a number of tours celebrating LGBTQ+ history across everything from Victorian drag balls to the city’s famous pride parade and the queer activism that’s been present on the streets of Manchester for hundreds of years. There’s five dates from now until the end of Pride weekend, and what better way to mark it than to reflect on what happened on the very cobbles we walk on that made way for such a joyful celebration. Это история о мужчине и женщине. О случайной встрече, которая постепенно превращается в откровенный разговор — честный, смешной, ранимый и очень человеческий. О том моменте, когда между людьми исчезают роли и, наконец, становится невозможно притворяться. На сцене — Алексей Панин и Ольга Силина. Тонкая актерская игра, живая энергия и удивительно узнаваемая история, в которой каждый услышит что-то своё. “Скамейка” — спектакль, после которого хочется немного помолчать и еще долго думать о главном. Если вам не хватает настоящего театра — этот вечер нельзя пропустить. Количество билетов ограничено. candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.evidence_text: Cyber start-up raises $7 million to tackle AI risk | Bdaily Ben Armstrong, left, and Thomas Ballin, founders of Cytix Cyber start-up raises $7 million to tackle AI risk A Manchester-based cybersecurity start-up has secured $7 million to accelerate the rollout of technology designed to tackle emerging risks created by rapid software development. Cytix has completed a Series A funding round led by Northern Gritstone, with participation from existing investors Auriga Cyber Ventures and NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance. The latter is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II. Bosses say the investment will support the rollout of Cytix’s newly launched change risk platform, which monitors software changes and updates to identify and validate potential security risks. They add the technology responds to growing pressure on organisations to keep security controls aligned with increasingly rapid software development, as AI-assisted coding, agentic workflows and continuous delivery accelerate the volume and pace of change. Ben Armstrong, chief executive of Cytix, said: “We chose Northern Gritstone for their conviction in investing in deeptech companies in the North of England with global ambition. “Northern Gritstone and Cytix share the belief that software change is becoming a key risk for organisations and those that build software need a solution that scales with the current pace of development. “We’re also grateful to the existing investors that have backed us since the early days and increased their commitment because they've seen the thesis play out.” Ben added: “Software is changing. “AI-assisted development means change now happens at machine speed. Meanwhile, very few security leaders have control over, or understanding of, those changes from a risk perspective. “Right now, existing tools can tell you what vulnerabilities you have, but can’t tell you about the risk. “We launched Cytix’ change risk management platform to get control of that risk.” Cytix’s platform, which entered general release yesterday (August 12), sits between a customer’s software development processes and its risk, security and compliance functions. It analyses what has changed, assesses the potential business risk, determines what security action is required and provides evidence showing how that risk was managed. The company says this can help organisations maintain oversight as increasing volumes of AI-generated code enter their systems. The funding will also help Cytix expand among enterprise and regulated businesses, where demonstrating effective governance of software changes can be a compliance requirement. Customers can access the technology directly through Cytix or via managed service partnerships with NCC Group and KPMG. Duncan Johnson, chief executive of Northern Gritstone, added: “The explosion of AI-assisted software development has led to a race to ensure software implementation remains secure. “Cytix’s platform aims to help enterprises take a realistic approach, recognising where change carries the most risk whilst allowing businesses to innovate. Northern Gritstone is proud to support another ambitious Manchester-based business in an exciting phase of its growth.” Sarah Isal, principal investor at Auriga Cyber Ventures, added: “We invested in Cytix because the team identified early that software change would become a critical cybersecurity challenge. “Since then, they’ve shown the resilience and discipline to execute on that vision, building a product that’s earning the trust of enterprise customers and strategic partners alike. “We’re proud to continue supporting Ben, Thomas and the team in this next phase of growth.” The £660 million NPIF II fund, which is operated by the British Business Bank, provides loans from £25,000 to £2 million and equity investment up to £5 million to help a range of small and medium sized businesses, driving innovation and creating opportunities for businesses to grow, scale, and thrive. Sue Barnard, senior investment manager at the British Business Bank, added: “Cytix is a great example of the ambitious technology businesses emerging from the North of England, developing innovative solutions to address the challenges created by the rapid growth of AI and software development. “Through the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II, we’re supporting businesses like Cytix that align with the Government’s Modern Industrial Strategy, helping to strengthen the North’s thriving

candidates.evidence_text: A new exhibition coming to The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Opening this October, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

candidates.evidence_text: From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ 11 April-11 July 2026 View dates and times Date Time Session Features 11 Apr 2026 10:30 am-12:30 pm 11 Jul 2026 10:30 am-12:30 pm Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Is there any place in the UK that has changed so quickly and so utterly as Ancoats ? From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: @ The Blues Kitchen Manchester on Every Friday Every Friday night, The Blues Kitchen Manchester turns up the heat with RnB, Hip Hop and Afrobeats 'Til Late party. The evening kicks off early downstairs at 7pm with a laid-back, candlelit soundtrack of live soul and neo-soul. But as the clock strikes 10pm, the main room transforms into a full-scale celebration as Manchester's finest DJs and live performers spin everything from old-school Lauryn Hill anthems to fresh, bass-heavy tracks from Burna Boy and Drake. The best part? It is completely free entry all night, meaning you can save your cash for the venue's legendary cocktails, private karaoke booths, and retro photo stands. If you happen to miss out on Friday's action, or you simply want to make it a double-header weekend of live music, don't worry - the venue hosts their equally electric sister event, Manchester Got Soul , where the legendary resident house band delivers three incredible live sets of timeless Motown, soul, and rock 'n' roll classics

It’ll be transformed into a full-on celebration of flowers, green spaces and the future of urban nature The Manchester Flower Festival is back from Saturday 23 to Monday 25 May 2026, taking over St Ann’s Square and King Street with bold floral displays, outdoor dining and a packed programme of events Now in its ninth year, it’s become one of those dates that people genuinely look forward to. The kind of thing that gets your camera roll filling up and reminds you just how good the city can feel in the sunshine This year’s theme is simple but powerful: Green Manchester It’s all about how the city is evolving. candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United Transfer News LIVE Updated 18 mins ago Man United transfer news LIVE: £19m striker eyed, Bruno Fernandes negotiations, Manu Kone latest Latest Manchester United transfer news with updates on Lewis Hall, Adam Wharton, Kim Min-jae, Louis Page and mo The big news on Monday was that Galatasaray are prepared to double Bruno Fernandes’s wages in a bid to lure him away from Manchester United. But as reported by the MEN , United will not entertain any offer for Fernandes in the final two weeks of the summer transfer window Fernandes rejected an approach from Saudi Arabia club Al-Hilal in favour of staying at United last year. However, he made headlines in December when he suggested United wanted him to join Al-Hilal United are also reportedly considering a move for Freiburg forward Igor Matanovic, valued at €22m (£19m), as Michael Carrick looks to bolster his attacking options. Matanovic's emergence is reportedly closely connected to Joshua Zirkzee’s situation at Old Trafford The Reds are continuing to work on other potential arrivals, with reports suggesting they are getting closer to completing a deal for exciting young midfielder Louis Page. It's claimed that United are close to agreeing a £10million plus add-ons deal with Leicester City for the 18 United have also reportedly turned their attention to Sander Berge and Joaquin Seys as they look to sign a midfielder and a left-back before the transfer deadline. Any move for Berge could come as a blow for Manu Kone and his hopes of moving to Old Trafford

candidates.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне В Лондоне прозвучит украинская песня, и снова найдет своих людей, ведь на сцену выйдет Наталка Карпа — певица, чей голос уже более двух десятилетий остается голосом света и искренней любви к родной земле. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! Чтобы попасть на концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 1 ноября 2026 года в Manchester Academy состоится концерт KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI в Манчестере Манчестер — город, где встречаются культуры, музыкальные традиции и люди из разных уголков мира. Именно здесь украинское хип-хоп трио KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI снова выйдет на сцену, чтобы презентовать свою новую музыку. Их песни для многих стали воспоминаниями о первой любви, важны За более чем десятилетие творчества KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI создали свой неповторимый стиль, в котором мелодичный рэп органично переплетается с проникновенной лирикой и откровенными жизненными историями. Миллионы прослушиваний, аншлаги в разных странах Европы и преданная аудитория Особого настроения событию придаст город Манчестер, который заслуженно считают одной из мировых столиц современной музыки. Здесь рождались легендарные группы, открывались культовые клубы и формировалась британская музыкальная сцена. Концерт украинского трио станет еще одной яркой В этот вечер KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI представят обновленную концертную программу, в которой свежие композиции будут звучать вместе с любимыми песнями поклонников. Вас ждет — живой звук, мощный речитатив, драйвовые мелодии, подпевающие весь зал, сотни фонариков и та самая неповтори Чтобы попасть на концерт KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI в Манчестере, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города.
